title: Use the Hospital exception path when a tipper cannot detect or clamp a tote (AGB) correctly
summary: When a tipper reports it cannot see the tote correctly (photo sensors) or cannot clamp/grip the tote fully, the system routes the item to the Hospital area for exception handling. This runbook turns that explanation into a live, observable check of (1) the detection/clamping failure symptoms and (2) the expected Hospital handling model (not continuously manned; supervisor/nearby tipper coverage).
when_to_use: Use when you observe/are told that a tipper cannot detect the tote correctly with its photo sensors (e.g., tote pushed back too far, toe on its side) or cannot clamp down fully (tries to grip but can’t), and you need to confirm the expected routing to the Hospital exception area and how Hospital is handled.
roles_and_responsibilities: L1_support: Perform the live observation checks of tipper detection/clamping symptoms and confirm the item is routed to the Hospital area; verify Hospital handling expectations (shared coverage, not continuously manned).
access_or_tools_needed: Live visibility of the tipper behavior (photo-sensor detection and clamp/grip attempt) and whether the item is routed to the Hospital area

system_preconditions: A tipper is attempting to handle a tote/AGB and is exhibiting detection and/or clamping/gripping failure symptoms.

visual_references.description: Training frame showing the Hospital exception handling explanation: photo-sensor detection failure or inability to clamp/grip fully sends the item to Hospital; also describes Hospital staffing as not continuously manned (supervisor bounces back and nearby tipper positions keep an eye).

steps.title: Identify the exception condition: tipper photo sensors cannot see the tote correctly or the tipper cannot clamp down fully
steps.purpose: Confirm the specific failure mode that the source ties to routing to the Hospital exception path.
steps.instruction: Observe the tipper handling attempt and determine whether the failure matches one of the source-described cases: (a) the tipper’s photo sensors cannot see the tote correctly (e.g., tote pushed back too far, toe on its side), or (b) the tipper cannot clamp down fully (it tries to grip but can’t).
steps.expected_result: You can point to an observable symptom consistent with either: photo-sensor tote detection failure or inability to clamp/grip fully during the tipper attempt.
steps.healthy_condition: The tipper attempt shows the described detection/clamping failure symptoms (photo sensors not seeing the tote correctly, or clamp/grip attempt cannot complete).
steps.failure_condition: The tipper attempt does not match the source-described detection/clamping failure symptoms (e.g., it clamps/grips successfully and/or photo sensors appear to detect the tote correctly).

actions.label: Check for photo-sensor detection failure symptom
actions.exact_action: Confirm whether the tipper’s photo sensors cannot see the tote correctly (e.g., tote pushed back too far, toe on its side).

actions.label: Check for clamp/grip failure symptom
actions.exact_action: Confirm whether the tipper cannot clamp down fully (it tries to grip but can’t).

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: If the tipper’s photo sensors can’t see the tote correctly (e.g., tote pushed back too far, toe on its side), the tipper sends it to the hospital. Other times, if it can’t clamp down fully (tries to grip it but can’t), it sends it to the hospital.

“...he’s got photo sensors... if it doesn’t see the tote right... then he sends... to the hospital... if it can’t clamp down fully, like it tries to grip it but can’t, then I’ll send it to the hospital.”

steps.title: Verify the system routes the item to the Hospital area when detection or clamping fails
steps.purpose: Confirm the expected routing behavior tied to the exception condition.
steps.instruction: After the tipper exhibits the source-described detection/clamping failure symptom, verify that the item is sent to the Hospital area (Hospital exception path).
steps.expected_result: The item is routed to the Hospital area as the exception handling destination following the tipper’s inability to detect the tote correctly or clamp/grip it fully.
steps.healthy_condition: Hospital routing occurs when the tipper cannot see the tote correctly or cannot clamp down fully.
steps.failure_condition: The item is not routed to the Hospital area despite the source-described detection/clamping failure symptoms.

actions.label: Confirm Hospital routing
actions.exact_action: Verify the item goes to the Hospital area after the tipper fails to detect the tote correctly or fails to clamp down fully.

stop_or_escalate_if: If the item is not being sent to Hospital despite the source-described detection/clamping failure symptoms, escalate for deeper troubleshooting beyond the source-provided explanation.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: If photo sensors do not see the tote correctly, or if the system cannot clamp down fully, it sends the item to the hospital.
“...then he sends... to the hospital... then I’ll send it to the hospital.”

steps.title: Confirm Hospital handling expectations: not continuously manned (supervisor bounces back and nearby tipper positions keep an eye)
steps.purpose: Set correct expectations for how Hospital items are handled so you don’t misinterpret the absence of a dedicated operator.
steps.instruction: When the item is in the Hospital area, verify that Hospital is handled according to the source model: there is not someone continuously standing at Hospital; a supervisor bounces back and forth, and nearby tipper positions keep an eye on Hospital items.
steps.expected_result: You observe/confirm that Hospital is handled via shared coverage (supervisor/nearby tipper attention) rather than a continuously manned station.
steps.healthy_condition: Hospital items are managed by supervisor/nearby tipper coverage; there is no dedicated always-on operator standing at the Hospital station.
steps.failure_condition: Hospital is treated as a continuously manned station (e.g., you expect a dedicated operator to be continuously present) and you misinterpret the situation; or Hospital handling does not match the shared-coverage model described by the source.

actions.label: Check for shared coverage behavior
actions.exact_action: Confirm that the supervisor bounces back and forth and nearby tipper positions keep an eye on Hospital items (i.e., not a continuously manned station).

stop_or_escalate_if: Do not assume the Hospital is manned continuously; if immediate human presence is expected, confirm the supervisor/nearby tipper coverage model described by the source.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: Hospital station is not continuously manned; the supervisor bounces back and forth and nearby tipper positions keep an eye on Hospital items.

“Do we have an operator at the hospital station? Yeah... the supervisor kind of bounces back and forth... there’s not somebody standing there... they handle the hospitals as they come through... trained the two tipper positions closest enough to keep an eye on the hospital... It’s not like a manned station.”

success_criteria: You can identify the source-described exception condition: photo-sensor tote detection failure and/or inability to clamp/grip fully.
The item is routed to the Hospital area when detection or clamping fails.
Hospital handling matches the source model: not continuously manned; supervisor/nearby tipper coverage.
healthy_conditions: Tipper exhibits the source-described detection/clamping failure symptoms (photo sensors cannot see tote correctly; clamp/grip cannot complete).
Item is sent to the Hospital area as the exception destination.
Hospital is handled via shared coverage (supervisor bounces back and nearby tipper positions keep an eye), not a continuously manned station.
failure_conditions: Item is not routed to Hospital despite the source-described detection/clamping failure symptoms.
Hospital handling expectations are incorrect (e.g., assuming a continuously manned station) leading to misinterpretation of the situation.
escalation_guidance: If the item is not being sent to Hospital despite the source-described detection/clamping failure symptoms, escalate for deeper troubleshooting beyond the source-provided explanation.
